gaps.sentence: Barely ___ the ink dried when the complaints began to arrive.
gaps.explanation: 'Barely had the ink dried when …' — inverted past perfect.

gaps.sentence: Hardly ___ the tenders been opened when the leak was traced to the press office.
gaps.explanation: 'Hardly had … been opened when' — past perfect passive with inversion.

gaps.sentence: So widespread ___ the outage that servers abroad noticed.
gaps.explanation: So widespread was the outage that… — inversion.

gaps.sentence: In no way ___ this report reflect the views of the editor.
gaps.explanation: In no way does this reflect… — formal disclaimer structure.

gaps.sentence: Not only ___ the play cancelled, but the theatre was closed as well.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only was the play cancelled' — inverted passive.

gaps.sentence: Were it not ___ the funding cuts, the library would still be open.
gaps.hint: were it not ___ = if it were not for
gaps.explanation: 'Were it not for' introduces the one thing preventing the outcome.

gaps.sentence: Hardly ___ anyone noticed the subtle change in the final scene.
Such ___ the chaos at the airport that hundreds slept on the terminal floor.
gaps.explanation: 'Such was the chaos that…' — emphatic fronting of 'such' with inversion.
